title: Renewal Dashboard Metric Primer
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a compact, practitioner-focused primer for the renewal dashboard: clear metric definitions, how we measure them, simple calculation examples, and a compact KPI table template managers can paste into reviews. Designed for account owners, CS ops, and SAs who need unambiguous signals for renewal conversations.

How to use this doc:
- Paste the KPI table into customer QBR slides and the renewal tracker spreadsheet.
- Use the measurement window guidance to align alerts and cohort queries.
- Follow the recommended severity -> action mapping for playbook steps.

Metric definitions and measurement guidance:
1) Request latency (end-to-end generation latency)
  - Definition: wall-clock time from when a customer request enters Redwood’s front-door (ingress timestamp) to when the final token is delivered to the client or response stream closed. Counts server-side processing + network queuing in our edge region.
  - Dimensions to slice by: model, route (chat/generate/embedding), region, customer-plan (hosted/dedicated/private), sequence-length bucket (<=128, 129-512, >512).
  - Typical quantiles to report: p50, p90, p95, p99. Use p95 for SLA-oriented signals and p50 to track usual experience.
  - Measurement window: rolling 7d for trends, 30d for SLA compliance, and 1h for incident detection.
  - Calculation (example): take per-request latency samples for the window and compute quantiles. Exclude retried requests and synthetic health-check pings.
  - Simple threshold examples: p95 latency < 350ms (target), p95 between 350-700ms (warning), p95 > 700ms (critical). Tune by workload.

2) Uptime / Availability
  - Definition: percentage of time in a measurement window that the customer’s configured endpoints return successful application-level responses (200-range for our API semantics) within an accepted timeout. We report both control-plane availability and data-plane availability.
  - Measurement window: 30d rolling for contractual SLAs, 7d for operational view.
  - Calculation (example): availability = 100 * (successful_responses / total_requests_within_window). Only count production traffic and exclude scheduled maintenance windows (annotated in the calendar).
  - Severity guide: availability >= 99.9% (green), 99.0-99.9% (amber), <99.0% (red) for high-tier customers. For lower tiers thresholds may be relaxed by 0.5-1.0%.

3) Cost per token (unit cost)
  - Definition: average server-side cost associated with tokens served (includes compute + GPU amortized + caching cost attribution for a simple model). Reported as USD per 1k tokens for clarity.
  - Measurement approach: attribute costs from the serving runtime by model and instance type, allocate by token counts observed in the same window. If a customer uses multiple models, compute a weighted average by token volume.
  - Calculation (example): cost_per_1k_tokens = (sum(compute_costs_for_window) / sum(tokens_served_in_window)) * 1000. Round to 3 decimal places for reporting.
  - Typical targets: For interactive chat workloads, aim for <= $0.20 per 1k tokens on optimized configs; for long-context inference >512 tokens, expect higher unit costs. Use Optimize recommendations to find savings.

4) Cache hit rate (prefix/KV cache effectiveness)
  - Definition: fraction of generation requests that benefited from an applicable cache entry (prefix, KV or response cache) such that the request avoided equivalent full model compute.
  - Measurement nuance: cache schemes vary (prefix vs response vs KV); report both a combined hit rate and per-cache-type breakdown. Also report effective token savings (tokens avoided) alongside hit rate.
  - Calculation (example): hit_rate = 100 * (requests_served_from_cache / total_requests). tokens_saved = sum(estimated_model_tokens_skipped_due_to_cache).
  - Operational thresholds: combined hit_rate >= 12% (good for conversational workloads with repeated prompts), 5-12% (opportunity), <5% (low leverage). Sensitivity depends on product pattern.

KPI table template (compact, paste into slide or tracker)
- Column headings (single line): metric | primary_sample | period | target | current | delta | trend | owner | playbook_action
- Example rows (comma-separated for simple paste):
  "latency_p95, customer-visible p95 (ms), 30d, <350, 472, +122, worsening, Aisha Patel, run Verify-latency-strikebook + scale-dedicated-pool"
  "availability_30d, data-plane availability (%), 30d, >=99.9, 99.82, -0.08, flat, Marco Ruiz, investigate-region-fallsback-and-contact-SRE"
  "cost_per_1k, USD per 1k tokens, 30d, <=0.20, 0.264, +0.044, rising, Evelyn Zhang, apply-Optimize-profile-3 and enable-cache-prefetch"
  "cache_hit_combined, combined cache hit rate (%), 30d, >=12, 7.4, -1.2, falling, Noah Singh, run-cache-analysis-and-suggest-prompt-refactors"

Notes on the KPI table fields:
  - primary_sample: short descriptor for the metric (what we show in customer slides).
  - period: reporting window (1h, 7d, 30d).
  - delta: current - target (show sign explicitly, e.g., +0.12 if above target when metric is worse).
  - trend: one of improving / worsening / flat / volatile. Compute from slope of daily points; if unclear mark volatile.

Severity mapping -> operational actions (playbook snippets)
  - Latency: warning (p95 > target) -> notify account owner, enable short-term burst capacity, schedule root-cause triage within 24h.
  - Latency: critical (p95 >> target or p99 spike) -> open incident, ramp dedicated capacity or route to lower-cost model variant, inform customer-facing lead.
  - Availability: any sustained drop below tier target -> incident and rollback policy evaluation, escalate to SRE and Legal if contractual breach expected.
  - Cost: cost-per-1k rising by >20% QoQ -> cost review, recommend batching/quantization/quantized-model variant.
  - Cache: rapid fall in cache hit rate -> analyze prompt variance, recommend canonical prompt templates, evaluate cache TTLs and prefetch population jobs.

FAQ and measurement gotchas:
- Synthetic tests can inflate availability but not reflect user experience; always cross-check with production traffic sample.
- Small customers with low request volumes will see volatile quantiles; use moving windows and annotate low-volume rows in the tracker.
- When customers have mixed deployment types (private + hosted), show split KPIs per deployment type and a consolidated weighted line.
- Cost attribution is an estimate; for contractual billing link back to raw invoice lines.

Appendix: short SQL snippets (pseudo) for common queries:
- p95 latency by model for last 7d: SELECT model, percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY latency_ms) AS p95 FROM requests WHERE ts > now() - interval '7 days' AND env = 'prod' GROUP BY model;
- combined cache hit rate: SELECT 100.0 * sum(case when served_from_cache then 1 else 0 end) / count(*) AS hit_rate FROM requests WHERE ts > now() - interval '30 days' AND env = 'prod' AND customer_id = :cust;
- cost per 1k tokens: SELECT (sum(allocated_cost_usd) / nullif(sum(tokens),0)) * 1000 AS cost_per_1k FROM cost_allocations WHERE window = '2025-01' AND customer_id = :cust;

Suggested next steps for the account team:
- Paste the compact KPI table into the renewal tracker and set owners for each metric.
- Run a 30-day batch job to compute the baseline numbers used above and share a short one-pager with the customer ahead of the review.
- Iterate threshold values with the customer during the next review and save them as per-customer config in the renewal tracker.
